reason: The only available combination pairs the hose and pump, which seem useful for moving recovered water to the garden.
expectation: I expect them to form a pumped water line, though it may still need connecting to the garden service port.

effect: The hose and pump formed a return loop that splashes water into the reservoir before sending it back to the beds. Connecting it at the garden port looks like the remaining step.
reaction: The splash was an interesting detail; I had expected a pumped line but not that arrangement.
reason: The garden service port is the only offered gameplay connection and seems like the natural place to install the return loop.
expectation: I expect the loop to connect the treated dehumidifier water to the garden, completing the moisture-return goal.

effect: The installation completed the moisture-return goal. I now understand that treated condensate enters through a nutrient doser while water from both beds drains back through the aerating return.
reaction: It was satisfying to see water from the window feeding the garden again, though I was curious about how the nutrient doser regulates the mixture.

mostWorthwhile.text: Installing the return loop was most worthwhile because it connected the condensation, treatment, nutrient dosing and garden into a visible cycle.

leastWorthwhile.text: Combining the hose and pump felt fairly predictable, though the resulting splash added an interesting detail.

surprise.text: I expected a pumped line, but the return loop splashes water above the reservoir surface before sending it back to the beds.

arbitrary.text: Neither action felt arbitrary: the hose and pump suggested moving water, and the garden port was a natural connection point. Both were the only gameplay options offered at their respective steps.

continue.text: I would continue because I am curious how the crops develop and how the expedition makes use of its other systems.
